mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 0.5% within the last month signals a loosening of monetary policy, which typically leads to increased liquidity in the market and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances where FEDFUNDS decreases by more than 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3 percentage points within the last month signals a weakening labor market, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where UNRATE increases by more than 0.3 percentage points.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over the last three months signals strong consumer demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where RSAFS shows sustained growth.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% over the last three months signals a contraction in supply, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where INDPRO decreases by more than 2%.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in a month, it signals inflationary pressure and tightening monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL increases by more than 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4% and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in a month, it signals a tight labor market and potential wage inflation, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4% and PAYEMS increases > 200k in 1 month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where UNRATE < 4% and PAYEMS increases by more than 200,000.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over the last three months signals strong demand in the housing market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, especially during an economic expansion.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where HOUST shows sustained growth during an economic expansion.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) is growing at a rate of more than 3% annually and GDP (GDPC1) growth is below 2% in the same period, it signals a supply-side mismatch, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO growth > 3% annually and GDPC1 growth < 2% annually
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where INDPRO growth exceeds 3% annually and GDPC1 growth is below 2% annually.
